question.problem:
Find the solution to the initial value problem

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t)-3{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-{x}_{1}(t)+4{x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned},\,x(1)=[\begin{aligned}5{e}^{2} \\ 3{e}^{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

*Hint: The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are ${\lambda }_{1}=5$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=1.$*
question.worked_solution:
First, we write down the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)$ for the given system:

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}]
$$

We need to find the eigenvalues and the eigenvectors of the matrix $A.$

- We are given that the eigenvalues are

$$
{\lambda }_{1}=5\,\text{and}\,{\lambda }_{2}=1.
$$

- Let's go through the process of finding the eigenvectors.

- For ${\lambda }_{1}=5,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{1}I=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -3 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

- For ${\lambda }_{2}=1,$ we get 

$$
A-{\lambda }_{2}I=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

So, we get an eigenvector 
${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

Now, we write down the general solution to the given linear system of differential equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t} \\  & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the values of ${c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{2}.$ Substituting $t=1$ into the general solution, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(1) & =[\begin{aligned}5{e}^{2} \\ 3{e}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\ {c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{5}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]e & =[\begin{aligned}5{e}^{2} \\ 3{e}^{2}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-{e}^{5}{c}_{1}+3e{c}_{2} \\ {e}^{5}{c}_{1}+e{c}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5{e}^{2} \\ 3{e}^{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have a system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}-{e}^{5}{c}_{1}+3e{c}_{2}=5{e}^{2} \\ {e}^{5}{c}_{1}+e{c}_{2}=3{e}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Adding the equations, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}4e{c}_{2}=8{e}^{2}\,⟹\,{c}_{2}=2e.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting ${c}_{2}=2e$ into the second equation, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{5}{c}_{1}+e(2e)=3{e}^{2}\,⟹\,{c}_{1}={e}^{-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the solution to the initial value problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & ={e}^{-3}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{5t}+2e[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}\end{aligned}
$$
